text:
maya: Heads up — we're seeing multi-minute gRPC stream stalls from pod -> pod on GPU nodes in us-west-2 after the midnight autoscale event. Streams just hang, no error, connection stays ESTABLISHED. :confused:

ton y: ugh, same cluster? which nodepool?

maya: yes. gpu-pool-v2, about 12 pods affected. Happens on long-lived streaming RPCs (log tailing & realtime infer). Short requests OK.

li: can you paste netstat / ss for a hung conn? also tcpdump on node nic?

maya: attaching quick sample: ```tcpdump: listening on eth0, link-type EN10MB (Ethernet) 12:34:56.789012 IP 10.2.5.12.50052 > 10.2.30.8.39234: Flags [.], seq 12345:12567, ack 9876, win 129, options [nop,nop,TS val 345678 ecr 123456], length 222```

akeem: interesting — packet sizes look ~220 bytes but we saw bursts of MSS-sized segments earlier. Any PMTU sysctl changes during scale?

julia: infra-bot reported a node drain + new instances spun up at 00:12 for scaling. opsbot showed kernel upgrades rolled to 5.15. Might be NIC driver/firmware interplay.

maya: checked dmesg on one impacted node: ```[    1.234567] igb 0000:3b:00.0: eth0: NIC Link is Up 10000 Mbps Full Duplex, Flow Control: Rx/Tx``` then later ```NETDEV WATCHDOG: eth0: transmit queue 0 timed out``` then some RX/GRO/GSO warnings.

tony: that screams offload + MTU mismatch. Did the CNI or cloud provider change overlay MTU? We pushed a Calico change last week but it shouldn't affect node MTU.

li: can someone run `ethtool -k eth0 | egrep -i "gso|gro|tso|sg|lro"` on affected nodes? and `ip link show` to check MTU?

maya: ran both on node-12: ```ip link show eth0 mtu 1500 qdisc mq state UP ...``` and `ethtool -k` shows gso/gro/tso: on.

akeem: overlay could be reducing effective path MTU (e.g., ENI + vxlan + ipsec). If GSO produces giant packets that get fragmented mid-path, some switches/firmware drop reassembly fragments, causing stream stalls with gRPC's long windows.

julia: noticed this pattern before — when PMTU blackholes happen, TCP stays ESTABLISHED but the application stalls silently until retransmit bursts. gRPC's keepalive might not trigger quickly.

li: quick mitigation — disable GSO/TCP segmentation offload on host NICs for GPU nodes: `sudo ethtool -K eth0 gso off tso off gro off`. Try on one node and see if streams recover.

maya: rolling onto a canary node now. Update: after toggling offoff, streams resumed immediately. gRPC latency back to normal. :raised_hands:

tony: ok so likely offload + MTU path issue. Need root cause: where is MTU being reduced? check host route MTU, VPC ENI config, and any in-path encapsulation (geneve/vxlan/ipsec).

akeem: AWS us-west-2 recently enabled ENA driver update on some instance types; their GSO handling can differ. Also we saw a kube-proxy ipvs change in the kernel release notes. Could be the kernel + nic driver mismatch.

julia: action items: 1) roll GSO off on all gpu-pool-v2 nodes as hotfix, 2) add monitoring for GRO/GSO errors in dmesg, 3) run packet captures with `tcpdump -s0 -w /tmp/grpc-hang.pcap port 50052` on both ends to confirm reassembly fragments, 4) engage cloud networking on possible PMTU changes.

li: adding a short-term k8s node bootstrap script to disable offloads for GPU node images. Also adding a kubelet `--max-pods` test to force different path? probably unnecessary.

maya: I've implemented the hotfix and sts pods recovered. Ops ticket opened: #NET-4122 to track driver/firmware reconciliation + testing matrix for NIC offload + kernel combos.

tony: long-term we need: e2e tests for long-lived gRPC streams across autoscale/drain events + synthetic PMTU/fragmentation tests. Add to infra backlog.

akeem: also consider enabling gRPC keepalive tuning to detect stalls faster and failover to alternate endpoints. But that's app-level, not root cause.

julia: pinging cloud-net team: @opsbot can you escalate to networking with trace info and pcap?

opsbot: Ticket NET-4122 created and escalated to cloud-networking. Assigned to @net-guardian.

maya: thanks all. leaving the canary offload disabled. Will follow up with postmortem once cloud team confirms root cause. :bookmark_tabs:
